messages.content: I have the St. Louis installation dates now. The condition review is Tuesday, July 14 at 1:30 p.m., and installation is Wednesday the 15th. They expect to finish around 5:00, but that could move. I need to work out flights from Atlanta before I look at hotels.

I can compare a Monday evening arrival with an early Tuesday nonstop, then look at both Wednesday evening and Thursday morning returns. Will you be traveling alone, and is the museum in the central city rather than out in the county?
Alone. The museum is in Forest Park. I need enough time to get from the airport, leave my bag somewhere, and be at the review without rushing.

That makes the Tuesday arrival possible, but less forgiving. From St. Louis Lambert to Forest Park, allow about 25 to 35 minutes by car in ordinary traffic, plus time to get off the plane and collect any checked case. A Monday arrival would remove weather and morning-delay risk and let you go directly to the museum Tuesday.
Show me actual workable combinations. Monday cannot be before 5:30 p.m. because I have to be at the Atlanta museum that afternoon.

For Monday, July 13, the strongest nonstop is Delta departing Atlanta at 6:25 p.m. and arriving in St. Louis at 7:05 p.m. local time. There is also an 8:40 p.m. departure arriving at 9:20 p.m. For Tuesday, Delta has a 7:10 a.m. nonstop arriving at 7:50 a.m. Either Tuesday flight timing leaves several hours before the 1:30 p.m. review, but the 7:10 departure would require an early airport arrival in Atlanta.
The 6:25 Monday flight is more sensible. What do the returns look like after the Wednesday work?

The relevant Wednesday nonstops are Delta at 7:35 p.m., arriving Atlanta at 10:05 p.m., and Delta at 9:05 p.m., arriving at 11:35 p.m. If installation ends at 5:00 sharp, the 7:35 could work, but only with a prompt departure from Forest Park. A 30-minute overrun, object signoff, or rush-hour traffic would make it uncomfortable. The 9:05 provides a better margin, though it creates a late arrival home.
And Thursday morning? I do not want to stay half the day Thursday.

On Thursday, July 16, Delta has nonstops at 7:15 a.m., arriving Atlanta at 9:45 a.m., and 9:40 a.m., arriving at 12:10 p.m. The 7:15 gets you home early but would mean leaving a Forest Park hotel around 5:30 a.m. The 9:40 permits a more ordinary morning and still returns you shortly after noon.
Compare the total fares for Monday at 6:25 paired with Wednesday at 9:05, Thursday at 7:15, and Thursday at 9:40. Regular economy, not the stripped-down fare.

In Delta Main Cabin, the current round-trip totals are $386.20 with the Wednesday 9:05 p.m. return, $354.20 with the Thursday 7:15 a.m. return, and $372.20 with the Thursday 9:40 a.m. return. All three include standard seat selection and a carry-on; a checked bag would be additional unless covered by status or an eligible card. These are current prices, not holds.
So staying Wednesday night is actually less expensive than flying out late Wednesday?

On airfare alone, yes: the Thursday 7:15 pairing is $32 less, and the Thursday 9:40 pairing is $14 less. The extra hotel night reverses that overall unless the Wednesday flight's operational margin is worth more than the lodging cost. The Wednesday 9:05 is viable, but it still depends on installation and signoff finishing by roughly 6:30 so you can leave for the airport.
The signoff is exactly what worries me. It can easily take forty-five minutes after the last object is placed. I should not build the trip around getting out Wednesday.

Then Thursday is the sounder anchor. Between the two morning choices, the 7:15 minimizes time away and costs the least, while the 9:40 avoids a very early departure and costs $18 more. Both remove the risk that Wednesday's work forces a flight change.
Use the 7:15 Thursday for the comparison. What are the seat options on those two flights?

On the Monday 6:25 p.m. outbound, Main Cabin currently has several standard windows in the rear half, including 22A, 23F, and 25A. On the Thursday 7:15 a.m. return, standard windows include 19A, 21F, and 24A. Preferred and Comfort+ seats cost extra. Seat availability can change until ticketing.
Window, please. Put 22A outbound and 19A back into the proposed itinerary.

I have the proposed pairing as Delta Main Cabin: Monday, July 13 at 6:25 p.m. from Atlanta, arriving St. Louis at 7:05 p.m., with 22A selected if still available; returning Thursday, July 16 at 7:15 a.m., arriving Atlanta at 9:45 a.m., with 19A selected if still available. The current fare is $354.20 round trip.
Do not book yet. I need to send the flight amount to the registrar. For the hotel search, what dates should I use, and is Monday evening late enough that I need to warn the hotel?

Use Monday, July 13 through Thursday, July 16: three nights, one adult, with checkout early Thursday morning. A 7:05 p.m. landing should put you at a Forest Park-area hotel around 8:00 to 8:30 p.m., so it is not generally a late arrival. Adding an estimated arrival time is still useful, especially if the property has limited front-desk hours.
Good. Anchor the hotel search to that. Give me a concise note I can send with the fare and explain why Thursday is the working return.

Proposed St. Louis flights, pending approval: Delta Main Cabin from Atlanta on Monday, July 13 at 6:25 p.m., arriving 7:05 p.m.; return Thursday, July 16 at 7:15 a.m., arriving Atlanta at 9:45 a.m. Current round-trip fare is $354.20, before any checked-bag fee, with standard seat selection included. The Thursday return is recommended because Wednesday installation is expected to end around 5:00 p.m. and object signoff may take another 45 minutes, leaving insufficient dependable margin for an evening flight. No flight has been booked or held. The hotel search should use July 13-16 for one adult near Forest Park.
